overview.summary: Full architectural integration protocol between Wnode (sovereign compute network) and Base, a secure, low-cost, developer-friendly Ethereum Layer 2 scaling network built on the open-source OP Stack by Optimism. The network implements a rollup architecture using the Optimism Bedrock design, featuring interactive fraud proofs via the Cannon fault-proof system, a reliable sequencer infrastructure transitioning toward decentralized sequencing topologies, and a standard EVM execution environment backed by Ethereum L1 security.
overview.why_it_matters: Operating compute workloads over an L2 like Base demands continuous, deterministic monitoring of transaction execution states, Optimistic Rollup state commitments, and L1/L2 gas market fluctuations. Because Base features a unique dual-layer gas fee configuration (L2 execution fee plus L1 data fee based on EIP-4844 blobs), automated agents require exact state observability to protect execution margins, track potential sequencer stalls, observe batch submission windows, and verify optimistic finalized states.
overview.integration_value: This integration enables sovereign Wnode agents to handle high-frequency off-chain data processing, trust-minimized state checks, and cross-chain operations with native access to Base. By combining deterministic runtimes with Base's scalable execution layer, developers can run fast, MEV-protected automations, monitor state bridging flows, and manage decentralized physical or financial applications with complete security.

endpoints.name: eth_getBlockByNumber
endpoints.returns: Full JSON-RPC block object matching the OP Stack execution payload specification, including standard L2 block metrics.

endpoints.name: eth_getLogs
endpoints.params: filterObject (JSON containing fromBlock, toBlock, address, and topics array)
endpoints.returns: Array of log objects matching contract event signatures emitted within the specified block interval.

endpoints.name: eth_call
endpoints.params: transactionCallObject (JSON containing to, data, gas fields), blockParameter (string)
endpoints.returns: The return value of the executed contract call encoded in hex format.

endpoints.name: eth_sendRawTransaction
endpoints.params: signedTransactionData (string, hex encoded compiled transaction byte string)
endpoints.returns: The 32-byte transaction hash identifier generated by the L2 sequencer pool.

endpoints.name: eth_estimateGas
endpoints.params: transactionCallObject (JSON containing from, to, data, and value fields)
endpoints.returns: Hexadecimal value representing the estimated L2 gas units required to run the transaction payload.

event_streams.description: Emitted whenever a matching event topic filter is caught in a new L2 execution block.
Fires if the delta between the L2 clock time and the latest received block timestamp exceeds standard 2-second block intervals.
Triggered when either Base L2 baseFee or underlying L1 data fee factors exceed user-defined standard deviations.
Triggered when a cross-domain message or bridge relay action (StandardBridge) remains unfinalized past standard roll-up checkpoint delays.

auth.method: API keys, Ethereum private key signing, EIP-1559 transaction model
auth.keys_required: Valid Base RPC Endpoint API Key (e.g., Node Provider Auth Token) and an ECDSA secp256k1 private key containing ETH on Base to cover gas fees.
auth.rate_limits: Standard RPC endpoints allow up to 600 requests per minute. Dedicated enterprise channels support up to 10,000 requests per minute.

pipelines.name: automated_contract_event_ingestion
pipelines.description: Maintains a constant socket loop over specific target EVM smart contracts on Base, matching runtime parameters against custom event signatures.
steps: Establish continuous polling connection using eth_getLogs for the recent block range.
Match log entries against target_contract_address and verify the structural validity of event_topic_hash.
Decode parameters locally inside the secure Wnode Wasm environment using the target contract ABI.
Format the parsed log and pipe it to downstream consumer automation tasks.

pipelines.name: automated_bridging_monitor
pipelines.description: Monitors native Layer 1 to Layer 2 cross-domain message transfers, verifying successful processing through the OptimismPortal and L2StandardBridge contract deployments.
steps: Query Ethereum L1 RPC to verify inclusion and receipts of the native bridge tx payload.
Extract the explicit cross-domain message nonce from the log parameters.
Poll the Base L2 transaction index to track the paired eth_sendRawTransaction or deposit tx execution block.
Confirm that the credited funds match target_recipient_l2_address on the L2 state ledger.

pipelines.name: automated_gas_optimization
pipelines.description: Calculates real-time cost dynamics by looking at both L2 execution parameters and L1 data blob costs via the GasPriceOracle contract.
steps: Query read-only values from the L1 Gas Price Oracle contract located at 0x420000000000000000000000000000000000000F.
Extract getL1GasUsed and getL1Fee multipliers for the specified transaction data payload.
Fetch current L2 base fee requirements via eth_getBlockByNumber.
Compile exact maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas values to minimize overall transaction fee waste.

pipelines.name: automated_mev_safe_transaction_execution
pipelines.description: Prepares, checks, and routes transaction configurations using specialized RPC paths to shield operations from open mempool sandwich vectors.
steps: Simulate transaction execution using eth_call to check target slippage bounds.
Sign the verified payload with the Wnode agent's isolated secp256k1 key configuration.
Route the transaction directly through MEV-aware private relay endpoints (e.g., Coinbase private sequencer channels) to avoid standard public mempools.
Monitor block inclusion receipts to ensure zero transaction reversion patterns.

sovereign_compute_usage.trust_minimized_flows: Wnode nodes process transaction signals using consensus protocols that run independently of underlying nodes. This ensures that actions like auto-compounding or liquidations execute exactly as intended, without relying on centralized intermediaries.
sovereign_compute_usage.deterministic_execution: All state monitoring tasks, data decoding loops, and gas calculations execute within sandboxed WebAssembly execution environments. This isolates runtime operations from external state variations, delivering identical results across all validating nodes.
sovereign_compute_usage.agent_mesh_patterns: Independent processing agents divide and conquer network duties: one agent parses incoming block states, another monitors gas prices, and a third builds transaction bundles. They synchronize status updates across an encrypted peer-to-peer network to coordinate actions instantly.

use_cases.title: High-Frequency Automated Liquidity Management
use_cases.description: Wnode agents continuously analyze trading pools across Base decentralized exchanges like Aerodrome. When pool configurations shift, agents execute rebalancing actions through private MEV-shielded pathways to protect trade value.
use_cases.value: Eliminates value losses from front-running and optimizes yield performance by updating pool ranges the moment market conditions change.

use_cases.title: Cross-Chain DePIN State Synchronization
use_cases.description: Synchronizes physical device status data tracked on specialized rollups directly with financial settlement accounts on Base, ensuring balance tracking stays accurate.
use_cases.value: Reduces operational delays by connecting real-world hardware data to on-chain accounts with minimal latency and high security.

test_vectors.input_scenario: Sequencer downtime limits block updates for more than 60 seconds.
test_vectors.expected_pipeline_behavior: The Wnode framework catches the delay, generates a 'sequencer_lag_detected' event signal, pauses active execution flows, and redirects read traffic to fallback L1 state verification engines.

test_vectors.input_scenario: An L2 chain reorg changes the last 3 block heights due to an L1 batch challenge reset.
test_vectors.expected_pipeline_behavior: The agent identifies the block hash shift using its tracking loop, rewinds local states to the last verified checkpoint block, and recalculates unfinalized data pipelines cleanly.

deployment.requirements: Wnode Environment Core package v3.0+ equipped with an EVM JSON-RPC execution toolkit, dedicated mainnet connection routes to Base L2 nodes, and automated gas fallback modules.
